info.name: Healthmarg API
info.description:
Healthmarg REST API (/api/v1). Import together with local.postman_environment.json and select the "Healthmarg — Local" environment.

Kept in sync with docs/api.md: every branch that changes an endpoint updates this file. Never store real secrets here.

request.description: 200 {status:"ok", database, redis} when healthy; 503 {status:"degraded"} when MySQL (or an enabled Redis) is down. redis is "disabled" locally when REDIS_ENABLED=false.

exec: pm.test('reports database and redis state', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.keys('status', 'database', 'redis'); });
pm.test('404 with generic message', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(404); pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.eql('Route not found'); });

item.name: Auth
item.description:
EMAIL FEATURES ARE OFF FOR NOW (EMAIL_ENABLED=false): Register returns 201 and signs you in (409 EMAIL_TAKEN if the email exists); Verify email, Resend, Forgot password and Reset password return 404 until email is switched on.

Sign-up, email verification, sign-in (with 2FA), sessions and password reset.

Locally, emails are saved as HTML files in backend/.local/outbox/ (and the link is printed in the API log). Copy the `token` from a link into the matching environment variable.

The refresh token lives in an HttpOnly cookie that Postman keeps automatically. Refresh/Logout need `GET csrf` first (it sets csrfToken) and send an Origin header, like a browser.

request.description: Issues a CSRF token (body) + signed cookie. Needed before Refresh and Logout.

Email off (current): 201 + accessToken (saved automatically) and the refresh cookie, or 409 EMAIL_TAKEN. Email on: always 202, then open the verifyEmail file in backend/.local/outbox/ and copy the token into verifyToken.

exec: pm.test('201 (signed in, email off) or 202 (email on)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([201, 202]));
pm.test('always 202 (never reveals whether the email exists)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(202));

request.description: 200 + accessToken (saved automatically), or {mfaRequired, mfaTicket} if 2FA is on → run "Login: 2FA code".

exec: if (b.accessToken) { pm.environment.set('accessToken', b.accessToken); pm.test('signed in: access token saved', () => pm.expect(b.user).to.be.an('object')); }

if (b.mfaTicket) { pm.environment.set('mfaTicket', b.mfaTicket); pm.test('2FA step needed: ticket saved (run the 2FA request next)', () => pm.expect(b.mfaRequired || b.mfaSetupRequired).to.be.true); }
if (b.backupCodes) console.log('BACKUP CODES (store safely, shown once):', b.backupCodes.join('  '));

item.name: Media (public)
item.description: Image renditions for pages. Cached for a year; served with CORP same-site and a sandboxing CSP.

request.description: Widths: 480, 960, 1600 (or the original width when the image is smaller).

item.name: Admin · Media
item.description: Needs an admin session that passed 2FA (Auth → Admin login → 2FA code). Uploads are multipart: in "Upload image", click the file field and choose an image. The uploaded id is saved as mediaId. Limits: one file, up to MAX_IMAGE_MB (15 MB by default; the list returns it as limits.maxImageMb), 60 uploads per admin per hour. Postman always sends Content-Length (uploads without one get 411).

formdata.description: Pick a JPEG, PNG or WebP from your computer.

formdata.value: Child’s pose on a yoga mat

request.description: The file type is read from its bytes (JPEG, PNG, WebP only). Stored as WebP at 480/960/1600 px without EXIF/GPS. 201 = new; 200 + deduplicated:true = this exact file was already uploaded.

formdata.description: Pick a JPEG, PNG or WebP from your computer.

request.description: Choose the same file as above.

exec: pm.test('tells the page the upload limit', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().limits.maxImageMb).to.be.a('number'));

item.name: Articles (public)
item.description: Published articles only. A members article shows in full only with a signed-in Authorization header; otherwise a teaser (locked: true).

exec: pm.test('200 (or redirect for an old address)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Admin · Articles
item.description: Needs an admin session that passed 2FA, a conditionId (Admin · Conditions → Create) and a mediaId (Admin · Media → Upload). Run in order: Create → Save draft → Checklist → Publish. Every save sends the draftVersion it started from (saved automatically into the environment); a stale one gets 409 STALE_VERSION.

request.description: The whole draft every time (up to 1 MB). The same draft again writes nothing and returns the same version.
422 PUBLISH_CHECKLIST lists every problem when something is missing.
409 HAS_INBOUND_LINKS when published articles link here; send confirm: true to go ahead.
